source.ref: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/31402; AACR-Bench dataset.json rows 273, 274, 275, 276, 277, 278, 279, 281 (forbid seed row 1645 not used); licence MIT read from LICENSE and package.json at head; hand-checked 2026-10-23 by adjudicator after two blind vetters; head is an intermediate commit of the pull request: its next commit 93850e9b13 fixed row-276 and row-279, commit 18422b41c8 (merged as f3769ebafb) gave computeAsync() the dispatch size and upstream later made compute() forward it

rationale: The change lets compute nodes take a three-dimensional workgroup size and lets renderer.compute() take an explicit dispatch size. ADR-0036; two blind vetters and an adjudicator. row-279 is required at warning: at head the WGSL builder throws for any workgroup size that is not exactly three entries, a regression for one- and two-entry sizes that compiled before and that the repository's own ComputeBuiltinNode examples use, fixed by the author's next commit (author-fix). row-276 is required at suggestion: an explicit dispatch of one or two entries is silently ignored and the node's count-based dispatch runs instead (zero workgroups for a node built from a workgroup-size array), fixed in the same commit. row-275 is optional (a model's comment, outside the diff hunks but made reachable by the new parameter): compute() before initialization hands off to computeAsync() without the dispatch size; upstream fixed it. Dropped: row-273 (a null count gives dispatchCount 0, not NaN, and count-less kernels are the design upstream kept), row-274 (the [0, 0, 0] default is a deliberate sentinel for the count-based dispatch), row-277 (an explicit dispatch over the device limit is the caller's error, reported by WebGPU validation; the merged code does not clamp either), row-278 (the fallback does bind the node's whole backend data object instead of its dispatchSize, but undefined y and z take dispatchWorkgroups' default of 1, so the predicted runtime error does not happen, the stale y already existed at base, and the line went away in the later redesign rather than in a fix; adjudicated drop because no consequence remains, and not a forbid range because the wrong-object observation itself is accurate), row-281 (WGSL integer literals are abstract and convert to u32; upstream kept the code). Forbid seed row 1645 (deprecate the number form) is not used: a design suggestion outside the reviewers' contract rather than a false claim, upstream kept the number form, and its lines are row-279's alternate location.

expect.concern: The WGSL builder now throws unless the workgroup size has exactly three entries, so a compute node given a one- or two-entry size, which WGSL accepts, the previous code compiled, and the repository's own compute(512, [128]) examples use, fails to build.

An explicit dispatch size is honoured only when all three entries are positive, so a one- or two-dimensional dispatch such as [16] or [16, 16] is silently ignored in favour of the node's count-based dispatch, which is zero workgroups for a node created from a workgroup-size array.

When compute() runs before the renderer is initialized it hands off to computeAsync(), which takes no dispatch size, so an explicit dispatch is dropped and a node created from a workgroup-size array dispatches zero workgroups.
